suppress.notes: CVE-2026-47884 on the Spring Framework 6.2.19 jars, CVSS 9.8. NOT REACHABLE FROM THIS PROJECT. What it is: SSRF and RCE through Spring MVC's XsltView, when an application has a "/**" mapping that renders a view and the view name is not specified. The class is in spring-webmvc. Why it is not reachable here: the project renders no views at all. It is a JSON API and a set of fake operators: every handler returns data written by Jackson, and nothing resolves a view name, let alone an XSLT one. Evidence: no ViewResolver, View rendering, XsltView, XSLT or javax.xml.transform in any src/main; every controller is a @RestController (grep for @Controller finds none). ModelAndViewContainer appears once, as a parameter type in CallerArgumentResolver.resolveArgument, which is the signature the HandlerMethodArgumentResolver interface requires; nothing builds or renders a model and view. XsltView exists in the spring-webmvc jar and nothing references it. Checked 2026-11-07 on f5d3b1c, with the runtime dependency tree of every module (`mvn dependency:tree -Dscope=runtime`, per module) and the source of every module's src/main. The Spring modules this project ships are spring-core, -aop, -beans, -context, -expression, -jcl, -jdbc, -tx, -web and -webmvc, all 6.2.19. No runtime tree contains spring-webflux, spring-websocket, spring-messaging, reactor, Aalto, RSocket or Jetty. The scan matches the CPE spring_framework to every Spring jar at 6.2.19 and reports the finding on whichever it groups first: spring-core, then spring-tx, then spring-jcl, as each was suppressed in turn. So each entry covers the ten Spring jars this project ships, listed in its pattern, and not an eleventh that someone adds later. The code each CVE describes lives in a module or a feature this project does not ship or does not use. Until 2027-02-07Z: re-evaluate at the next Spring Boot upgrade, or on this date if there is none. The entry is pinned to 6.2.19 of the Spring jars this project ships, so any Spring bump on the Boot 3.5 line stops it matching and the finding comes back for a fresh decision. No fix exists on this line (6.2.19 is the newest 6.2.x); the advisories fix these in Spring 7 / Boot 4.

CVE-2026-59283 on the Spring Framework 6.2.19 jars, CVSS 9.1. NOT REACHABLE FROM THIS PROJECT. What it is: a guard bypass when SpEL expressions are evaluated with SimpleEvaluationContext while the SpEL compiler is active. The class is in spring-expression. Why it is not reachable here: no code in this repository evaluates a SpEL expression, so none is evaluated with SimpleEvaluationContext, and no request data reaches an expression. The SpEL compiler is Spring's default (off); nothing here turns it on. Evidence: no SpelExpressionParser, ExpressionParser, SimpleEvaluationContext, StandardEvaluationContext, @Value("#{...}") or @ConditionalOnExpression in any src/main, and no spring.expression.* property anywhere in the repository. spring-expression ships only as spring-context's dependency. I did not audit what each library in the tree evaluates internally; the claim is about this project's code and the data it passes. CVE-2026-59282 on the Spring Framework 6.2.19 jars, CVSS 7.5. NOT REACHABLE FROM THIS PROJECT. What it is: a denial of service when an application uses Spring's data binding to apply user-supplied property paths onto a target object. Why it is not reachable here: no request data is bound onto a bean through data binding. Handlers take a JSON body through @RequestBody, which Jackson reads, and otherwise only scalar strings from the path, the query or a header. Evidence: WebDataBinderFactory appears once, as an interface parameter of CallerArgumentResolver.resolveArgument, which never uses it. There is no @ModelAttribute, no @InitBinder, no DataBinder, BeanWrapper or BeanUtils in any src/main. All 32 handler methods in server and the simulators take only: ApiCredential (resolved by CallerArgumentResolver), @RequestBody, or @PathVariable, @RequestParam and @RequestHeader scalars (String, and Map<String, String> for headers). None takes an unannotated bean, which Spring would otherwise bind from the request as an implicit @ModelAttribute. CVE-2026-34479 on log4j-api and log4j-to-slf4j 2.24.3, CVSS 7.5 (CVSSv3; 6.9 under CVSSv4). FALSE POSITIVE. What it is: the Log4j1XmlLayout of the Log4j 1-to-Log4j 2 bridge (log4j-1.2-api), and the Log4j 1 compatibility layer's org.apache.log4j.xml.XMLLayout, fail to escape characters forbidden by XML 1.0. The scan matches the CPE apache:log4j to the log4j jars by name, and reports it on log4j-api, or on log4j-to-slf4j once log4j-api alone was suppressed. Why it is not reachable here: the vulnerable classes are not in what this project ships. Evidence: checked 2026-11-07 on f5d3b1c. log4j-api arrives only through log4j-to-slf4j, which Spring Boot's logging starter brings to route Log4j API calls to SLF4J; neither log4j-1.2-api nor log4j-core is in any module's runtime dependency tree, and neither log4j-api-2.24.3.jar nor log4j-to-slf4j-2.24.3.jar contains Log4j1XmlLayout or org/apache/log4j/xml/XMLLayout. The advisory's fixed version, 2.25.4, is for the bridge. Until 2027-02-07Z: re-evaluate when log4j-api is next upgraded, or on this date if it is not. The entry is pinned to 2.24.3 of the two log4j jars this project ships, so an upgrade stops it matching.
